title: Apple Launches $50 AI Usage Packs for Intelligence Tier
summary: Apple introduces $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs, its first paid Apple Intelligence tier, starting in Logic Pro and expanding to Final Cut Pro and iWork.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Apple launched $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs on November 5, 2026, marking its first paid Apple Intelligence tier available initially in Logic Pro.
- Unused credits roll over monthly and expire after 12 months, with no Family Sharing option and availability limited to eight countries at launch.
- The move ends Apple's free-only Apple Intelligence model as on-device usage hits monthly caps, with expansion to Final Cut Pro and iWork planned.


Apple officially launched $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs on November 5, 2026, introducing its first paid tier for Apple Intelligence. The one-time purchase initially works only inside Logic Pro, marking a shift from the company's all-free Apple Intelligence posture as on-device models encounter monthly usage caps.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 5, 2026, the Intelligence Usage Packs arrived via a Logic Pro update. Users access the purchase path through Logic Pro's menu bar: Intelligence Features, then Show Usage, then Buy More Usage. The packs currently function in only eight countries, with no Family Sharing support. Apple ties each pack to the Apple Account used for iCloud at the time of purchase.


## Pricing Structure and Credit Management


The $49.99 one-time pack provides additional Apple Intelligence usage beyond monthly limits, though Apple has not disclosed the exact amount of extra usage included. According to Apple's legal terms, unused additional usage purchased with intelligence usage packs roll over from month to month and expire 12 months after purchase. The extra usage only activates after a user exhausts their monthly allocation.


## Expansion Plans Across Apple's Creative Suite


Apple plans to extend Intelligence Usage Packs to Final Cut Pro, Pixelmator Pro, and the iWork suite later in November 2026. Future expansion could reach consumer-facing features including Siri, Image Playground, and Photos editing tools. The staggered rollout suggests Apple is testing pricing and usage patterns within professional creative applications before broader deployment.


## Strategic Context and Market Positioning


The launch ends Apple's free-only approach to Apple Intelligence, a shift the company had signaled earlier in 2026. The move arrives alongside multiple Apple AI developments, including reports that Apple may ship an agentic Siri version in 2027. By introducing paid tiers within professional apps first, Apple positions Intelligence Usage Packs as a power-user feature rather than a general consumer subscription.


## What This Means


Apple's first paid Apple Intelligence tier marks a strategic pivot from free on-device AI to a hybrid model that accommodates heavy usage. The one-time pack structure with 12-month expiration offers flexibility without recurring subscriptions, but the lack of Family Sharing and limited country availability signal a cautious, professional-first rollout. As Apple Intelligence features mature and expand across the ecosystem, additional pricing tiers targeting consumer applications are likely. The $49.99 entry point tests whether users will pay for extended AI access within creative workflows, setting precedent for broader Apple Intelligence monetization beyond hardware sales.
